articles.title: First Phosphate Reports 378% Surge in Indicated Mineral Resources
articles.summary: First Phosphate Corp (NASDAQ:PHOS) (OTC:FRSPF) on Monday filed an updated technical report revealing resource expansion at its Bégin-Lamarche project in Queb...
articles.body:
First Phosphate Corp (NASDAQ: PHOS ) (OTC: FRSPF ) on Monday filed an updated technical report revealing resource expansion at its Bégin-Lamarche project in Quebec, Canada.

The latest mineral resource estimate highlights a 378% surge in indicated resources compared to the company's initial assessment released on September 9, 2024.

Massive Resource Expansion At Bégin-Lamarche

The updated estimate demonstrates substantial resource growth for the deposit, located 50 kilometers northwest of Saguenay.

The technical report outlines 6.2 million tonnes of measured pit-constrained resources grading at 7.70% phosphate.

Furthermore, indicated resources reached 198.5 million tonnes at a 6.00% grade, while inferred resources hit 89.5 million tonnes at 6.16%.

Evaluators note that the deposit remains open at depth, allowing for potential future growth .

Recent metallurgical tests reveal a highly favorable projected apatite concentrate grade of 40.4% phosphate alongside an impressive 88% process recovery rate.

The extracted material contains minimal potentially harmful elements. Consequently, the concentrate successfully qualifies for the production of battery-grade phosphoric acid, a crucial component for lithium iron phosphate batteries, achieving a 91.1% conversion ratio.

Strategic Infrastructure And Offtake Agreements

The Bégin-Lamarche project benefits heavily from existing regional infrastructure.

The site sits adjacent to established road networks and hydroelectric facilities, operating only 70 kilometers driving distance from the deep-sea Port of Saguenay.

In August, First Phosphate's ADRs began trading on the Nasdaq Global Market. The company completed the uplisting without raising additional equity capital, providing broader access to U.S. investors without immediate dilution .

PHOS Stock Price Activity : First Phosphate shares were up 9.49% at $20.26 during premarket trading on Monday, according to Benzinga Pro data .

articles.title: Wheat Rallying on Monday Morning
articles.summary: Wheat is back to stronger trade on Monday morning, with contracts 7 to 13 cents higher. The wheat complex is in the red across the three exchanges on Friday....
articles.body:
Wheat is back to stronger trade on Monday morning, with contracts 7 to 13 cents higher. The wheat complex is in the red across the three exchanges on Friday. Chicago SRW contracts were fractionally to 1 ¼ cents lower on Friday, with September up 6 ¾ cents on the week. KC HRW futures posted losses of 1 ¾ to 6 cents on the session, with September holding onto a 2 cent gain for the week. MPLS spring wheat was down 2 ½ to 4 cents lower at the close, with September rallying 20 cents on the week.

articles.title: Nasdaq (NDAQ) Has Quietly Built a More Durable Business Beyond Trading
articles.summary: Guinness Global Innovators, an investment management company, recently released its Q2 2026 quarterly investor update for its “Guinness Global Innovators Fun...
articles.body:
Guinness Global Innovators, an investment management company, recently released its Q2 2026 quarterly investor update for its "Guinness Global Innovators Fund". You can download the letter here . The Guinness Global Innovators Fund focuses on investing in global companies that benefit from innovation in technology, communication, globalization, and management strategies. In the second quarter of 2026, the Guinness Global Innovators Fund returned 13.8% in GBP, compared with 13.0% for the MSCI World Index and 13.1% for the IA Global sector average. Easing Middle East tensions, falling oil prices, and renewed enthusiasm for artificial intelligence helped reverse much of the caution seen earlier in the year, with investors rotating back toward growth stocks and AI infrastructure beneficiaries. The Fund benefited from its overweight position in the Information Technology sector, while its overweight position in Communication Services detracted. Avoiding weaker Utilities, Materials, and Energy also supported relative performance. Also, please check the Fund's top five holdings to see its best picks for 2026.

In its second-quarter 2026 investor letter, Guinness Global Innovators Fund highlighted Nasdaq, Inc. (NASDAQ: NDAQ ) as a new holding. Nasdaq, Inc. (NASDAQ:NDAQ) operates as a technology company that serves capital markets and other industries. On August 21, 2026, Nasdaq, Inc. (NASDAQ:NDAQ) closed at $98.22 per share. One-month return of Nasdaq, Inc. (NASDAQ:NDAQ) was 4.56% and its shares gained 4.13% over the past 52 weeks. Nasdaq, Inc. (NASDAQ:NDAQ) has a market capitalization of $54.9 billion.

Guinness Global Innovators Fund stated the following regarding Nasdaq, Inc. (NASDAQ:NDAQ) in its Q2 2026 investor letter:

" Nasdaq, Inc. (NASDAQ:NDAQ) is best understood not as a traditional exchange but as a global technology, data, and analytics company that happens to own a major stock exchange, a positioning it has deliberately built since its 2017 strategic pivot away from transaction-driven revenue towards higher-growth, higher-margin software and analytics. Nasdaq's business is diversified across three segments. Through its Financial Technology segment, the firm is strategically positioned to benefit from a structural rise in compliance and transparency requirements as regulators demand more granular and frequent reporting from banks globally. This segment also houses Calypso, a trading and risk-management platform whose demand is underpinned by the growing complexity of trading, collateral, and risk requirements at large financial institutions. The Capital Access Platforms segment includes listing fees, market data subscriptions and index licensing on products such as the Nasdaq-100. Lastly, its exchange business, although originally the direct driver of the business, has become more of an enabler for other business segments, as trading activity generates proprietary pricing data that the company repackages and monetises, while providing the firm with a partial hedge during periods of heightened market volatility. Further, its 60% recurring revenue mix offers protection against economic downturns." ( Click here to read the full text )

articles.title: Michael Burry Is Shorting Nvidia Heading Into Earnings, Here’s What He’s Buying Instead
articles.summary: The man who called the 2008 housing collapse is walking into Nvidia's most consequential earnings report short the stock and long something Wall Street won't...
articles.body:
Burry called LULU "screaming cheap," doubling his stake to 17.4% of his portfolio while shorting NVDA at a $5.2 trillion valuation.

Burry's short book extends to QQQ and SOXX, but he refuses to short AAPL, calling it "permacostly" despite its rich valuation.

With 29 of 34 analysts rating LULU a Hold, Burry's contrarian bet on its forward P/E of 11 stands nearly alone on Wall Street.

Don't wait: the analyst who called NVIDIA in 2010 just revealed his top 10 AI stocks. See the full list FREE now .

Michael Burry is heading into the most important earnings report of the AI cycle positioned against it. NVIDIA ( NASDAQ:NVDA ) reports fiscal Q2 2027 results on Wednesday, Aug. 26, 2026, after the market close, and the Scion Asset Management founder spent the weekend on his Substack, Cassandra Unchained , defending a very different kind of stock. His comments were reported by Stocktwits reporter Prabhjote Gill on Monday, Aug. 24, 2026.

These were self-disclosures in a paid Substack chat, made in the days leading up to the single biggest quarterly release on the calendar for the AI trade. Riding a mania is one thing and planning the exit is another, which is exactly what we walked through in a free bubble survivor's handbook.

Burry has publicly discussed short positions involving Nvidia, Micron Technology, Oracle, Nebius, the iShares Semiconductor ETF and the Invesco QQQ Trust. That spans the AI capex complex, from the GPU designer to the memory supplier, the hyperscale software partner, the neocloud, and the two index vehicles most exposed to the theme.

Nvidia enters the report richly valued and richly expected. The stock closed Friday at $214.72, giving the company a market capitalization of roughly $5.2 trillion at a trailing P/E of 33. Last quarter, Nvidia posted revenue of $81.61 billion, up 85.23% year over year, with Data Center revenue of $75.25 billion and non-GAAP gross margin of 75.0%. Management guided Q2 to $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%, a number that excludes any Data Center compute revenue from China. The full Q1 FY27 release is on file with the SEC.

The centerpiece of his long book is Lululemon ( NASDAQ:LULU ). Burry wrote on Substack, "I believe LULU is screaming cheap here."

A reader in the Substack chat observed that he appeared to have nearly doubled his LULU position, and that it now accounts for 17.4% of his holdings versus 9% for Molina Healthcare, after adding to both. Tracking of his Substack disclosures also suggests larger long positions in Zoetis, MercadoLibre, JD.com and Adobe. Burry has said he moved his Alibaba position entirely into JD.com and would need Alibaba to fall by half before reconsidering.

articles.title: There are 6 stocks that both hedge funds and mutual funds have as overweight — and SpaceX is one
articles.summary: SpaceX, trading at 93 times next year’s estimated earnings, seems hardly the stock to unite both short-term-focused hedge-fund managers and more long-term-or...
articles.body:
SpaceX, trading at 93 times next year's estimated earnings, hardly seems the stock to unite short-term-focused hedge-fund managers and longer-term-oriented mutual-fund managers.

Yet according to Goldman Sachs's exhaustive look at $10 trillion in stock-market positions through 13-F filings with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, SpaceX SPCX is one of six stocks that both sets of portfolio managers have overweight positions in, relative to the S&P 500.

This has been one of the most affordable U.S. cities to buy a home for more than 134 years

The Treasury's bond-market intervention isn't working. So what comes next?

SpaceX went public on June 12, near the end of the second quarter, which the 13-F filings tracked.

The others: Boeing BA, Capital One Financial COF, Mastercard MA, Thermo Fisher Scientific TMO and Visa V.

It's an odd grouping but one that's handily outperformed the S&P 500 SPX this year, rising 29% versus 16% for the index, according to Goldman's calculations.

Goldman strategists led by Ben Snider say such "shared favorites" have since 2013 delivered an annual return of 17%, though they tend to be both volatile and trade at bigger price-to-earnings premiums.

These particular six stocks don't have much in common, even if two — Visa and Mastercard — operate in a near-duopoly in the global payments processing market, while Boeing is in a near-duopoly with France's Airbus FR:AIR in civil aviation.

Despite its heady valuation, SpaceX is the dominant player in both reusable commercial rockets and global satellite internet.

The Goldman analysis found that hedge funds were more exposed to stocks benefiting from artificial intelligence, while both sets of managers are overweight the financial sector XLF, for only the third time since Goldman started tracking that.

articles.title: XPeng Shares Fall After Q2 Miss as Robotics Unit Raises More Than $900 Million
articles.summary: XPeng (NYSE:XPEV) shares moved lower in U. S.
articles.body:
XPeng (NYSE:XPEV) shares moved lower in U.S. pre-market trading on Monday after the Chinese electric vehicle manufacturer reported second-quarter revenue and earnings below analyst expectations. The company also announced a major financing round for its robotics division, valuing the business at more than $6.3 billion.

XPeng reported a second-quarter loss of RMB1.29 per share, considerably wider than the RMB0.29 loss expected by analysts. Revenue reached RMB19.74 billion, an increase of 8% from a year earlier and 51.5% from the previous quarter, but below the consensus forecast of RMB20.57 billion.

The shares were down 3.5% by 06:49 ET (10:49 GMT).

Vehicle Revenue Rises as Gross Margin Improves

Vehicle sales generated RMB17.05 billion in revenue during the quarter, representing growth of 1.0% year on year and 55.0% quarter on quarter.

XPeng's overall gross margin strengthened to 20.7%, compared with 17.3% in the same period last year and 20.6% in the first quarter.

Vehicle margin, however, declined to 12.1% from 14.3% a year earlier and was unchanged from the preceding quarter.

Total vehicle deliveries reached 103,295 during the period, remaining broadly unchanged compared with the second quarter of last year.

XPeng Forecasts Up to 121,000 Deliveries for Q3

For the third quarter, XPeng expects to deliver between 115,000 and 121,000 vehicles.

That range would represent a year-on-year change of approximately negative 0.87% at the lower end to positive 4.30% at the upper end.

The company forecast third-quarter revenue of between RMB21.7 billion and RMB23.4 billion, implying annual growth of approximately 6.47% to 14.81%.

The guidance suggests XPeng expects sequential momentum to continue, although the relatively modest year-on-year delivery growth highlights the competitive conditions facing China's electric vehicle market.

XPeng Robotics Business Raises More Than $900 Million

Alongside its quarterly results, XPeng announced that its robotics operation had secured more than $900 million through a new financing round.

The transaction values the robotics unit at more than $6.3 billion on a post-money basis and represents a significant expansion of XPeng's ambitions beyond electric vehicles.

IDG Capital led the financing, with Gaorong Ventures also participating. Tencent and Alibaba joined the round as strategic investors.

According to XPeng, the transaction represents the largest single private funding round completed to date within China's embodied AI industry.

Funding Targets AI Development and Global Expansion

articles.title: Iran blacklists 45 tankers over Strait of Hormuz rules amid fresh US sanctions threat
articles.summary: International Business News: Iran has blacklisted 45 tankers for allegedly violating its rules for crossing the Strait of Hormuz and warned that vessels conducting ship-to-ship tr.
articles.body: Iran has blacklisted 45 tankers for allegedly violating its rules for crossing the Strait of Hormuz and warned that vessels conducting ship-to-ship transfers with them could also face action, escalating tensions over the key waterway nearly six months into the war.The Persian Gulf Strait Authority, a new body set up by Iran to manage the strait, said in an X post late on Sunday that the vessels could be fined, detained and have their cargoes confiscated.The list includes very large crude carriers, liquefied natural gas and liquefied petroleum gas tankers, and clean product vessels. Some are owned by the UAE's ADNOC Logistics and Shipping (ADNOC L&S), ADNOC subsidiary Navig8 Tankers and Saudi Arabia's national shipping carrier Bahri. Ships owned by Klaveness Ship Management, Stolt Tankers and South Korea's Sinokor are also included, according to Reuters.Which vessels are on Iran's blacklist?Kiku â IMO 9329796Mubaraz â IMO 9074626Minoan Pioneer â IMO 9471630Hafeet â IMO 9928009Al Rekayyat â IMO 9397339Wedyan â IMO 9524970Cyprus Prosperity â IMO 9595216Al Rawdah â IMO 9734513Rasheeda â IMO 9443413Lebrethah â IMO 9976927Lila Vadinar â IMO 9324100Maha Roos â IMO 9231004Gfs Galaxy â IMO 9401271Al Bahyah â IMO 9937799Mombasa B â IMO 9739501Stolt Magnesium â IMO 9739317Al Watan â IMO 9615030Navig8 Messi â IMO 9482859Singapore Prosperity â IMO 9419967Disha â IMO 9250713Gaslog Shanghai â IMO 9600528Lubna â IMO 9489065Hazi 1 â IMO 7802598Ryujin â IMO 8206818Anna Barbara â IMO 9407500Sunbird Arrow â IMO 9323821Minoan Dignity â IMO 9294484Maria â IMO 9917828Kavomaleas â IMO 1042823Mardan â IMO 9360453Sweden Prosperity â IMO 9588392Jarnain â IMO 9823546Kaifan â IMO 9656046Nissos Kea â IMO 9920758Rotterdam Energy â IMO 9508859Al Hamra â IMO 9074640Umm Al Ashtan â IMO 9074652Marigold Lng â IMO 9230062Banastar â IMO 9228045Navara â IMO 9241798Nissos Heraclea â IMO 9419618Blue Star 1 â IMO 9215115Ashley â IMO 9258464Mraweh â IMO 9074638Al Lulu â IMO 9583627Iran warns of harsh response to US sanctionsThe authority said ships involved in transfers with the blacklisted vessels could also be added to the list. It did not specify which rules had been breached. Iran has previously said shipowners should obtain clearance to transit the strait and pay for security and other services.The warning came days after the US threatened Iran with "the toughest sanctions in history". Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei warned of a harsh response.âAny escalation of this situation will undoubtedly bring about consequences,â Esmail Baghaei said. âOur hands are not tied.âIran's new top security official said support for the sanctions by any country would be considered an "act of war".Hormuz remains chokedThe US has imposed a naval blockade against Iran-related shipping. Before the conflict disrupted tanker traffic, the Gulf supplied about 20% of the world's daily crude oil and liquefied natural gas.Iran has said reopening the strait would require lifting the US blockade, withdrawing US forces from the region and reparations for war damage. It has also held talks with Oman on jointly managing the waterway.US-coordinated efforts to move tankers through the strait to fill supertankers waiting outside have helped restore some exports.US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said on X that the "7-day average of oil leaving the Strait is over 8 million barrels a day. Make no mistake, thanks to the U.S. Navy, oil is flowing through the Strait of Hormuz."Iran's currency hit a record low on Monday ahead of the expected US announcement. ADNOC declined to comment, while other shipping firms did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

Ships owned by Klaveness Ship Management, Stolt Tankers and South Korea's Sinokor are also included, according to Reuters.Which vessels are on Iran's blacklist?Kiku â IMO 9329796Mubaraz â IMO 9074626Minoan Pioneer â IMO 9471630Hafeet â IMO 9928009Al Rekayyat â IMO 9397339Wedyan â IMO 9524970Cyprus Prosperity â IMO 9595216Al Rawdah â IMO 9734513Rasheeda â IMO 9443413Lebrethah â IMO 9976927Lila Vadinar â IMO 9324100Maha Roos â IMO 9231004Gfs Galaxy â IMO 9401271Al Bahyah â IMO 9937799Mombasa B â IMO 9739501Stolt Magnesium â IMO 9739317Al Watan â IMO 9615030Navig8 Messi â IMO 9482859Singapore Prosperity â IMO 9419967Disha â IMO 9250713Gaslog Shanghai â IMO 9600528Lubna â IMO 9489065Hazi 1 â IMO 7802598Ryujin â IMO 8206818Anna Barbara â IMO 9407500Sunbird Arrow â IMO 9323821Minoan Dignity â IMO 9294484Maria â IMO 9917828Kavomaleas â IMO 1042823Mardan â IMO 9360453Sweden Prosperity â IMO 9588392Jarnain â IMO 9823546Kaifan â IMO 9656046Nissos Kea â IMO 9920758Rotterdam Energy â IMO 9508859Al Hamra â IMO 9074640Umm Al Ashtan â IMO 9074652Marigold Lng â IMO 9230062Banastar â IMO 9228045Navara â IMO 9241798Nissos Heraclea â IMO 9419618Blue Star 1 â IMO 9215115Ashley â IMO 9258464Mraweh â IMO 9074638Al Lulu â IMO 9583627Iran warns of harsh response to US sanctionsThe authority said ships involved in transfers with the blacklisted vessels could also be added to the list. It did not specify which rules had been breached. Iran has previously said shipowners should obtain clearance to transit the strait and pay for security and other services.The warning came days after the US threatened Iran with "the toughest sanctions in history". Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei warned of a harsh response.âAny escalation of this situation will undoubtedly bring about consequences,â Esmail Baghaei said. âOur hands are not tied.âIran's new top security official said support for the sanctions by any country would be considered an "act of war".Hormuz remains chokedThe US has imposed a naval blockade against Iran-related shipping. Before the conflict disrupted tanker traffic, the Gulf supplied about 20% of the world's daily crude oil and liquefied natural gas.Iran has said reopening the strait would require lifting the US blockade, withdrawing US forces from the region and reparations for war damage. It has also held talks with Oman on jointly managing the waterway.US-coordinated efforts to move tankers through the strait to fill supertankers waiting outside have helped restore some exports.US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said on X that the "7-day average of oil leaving the Strait is over 8 million barrels a day. Make no mistake, thanks to the U.S. Navy, oil is flowing through the Strait of Hormuz."Iran's currency hit a record low on Monday ahead of the expected US announcement. ADNOC declined to comment, while other shipping firms did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Stocking, speculation behind âunnaturalâ sugar price surge: ISMA
articles.summary: India Business News: NEW DELHI: Sugar industryâs apex body ISMA on Monday said that there is no shortage of the sweetener while admitting that the spike in prices is ânot .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Sugar industryâs apex body ISMA on Monday said that there is no shortage of the sweetener while admitting that the spike in prices is ânot naturalâ and is being fuelled by stocking by bulk consumers and âspeculative behaviourâ. The industry body said they want ârationalisationâ of retail prices and are hopeful of a reduction in the coming days following multiple steps that govt has taken.The industry also dismissed allegations of diversion of sugar for ethanol production as a reason for tight supply of the sweetener and increasing prices. It said only 290 crore litres out of a total 1,200 crore litre of ethanol came from sugar during this ethanol supply year (Oct 2025- Sept 2026). âOnly after ensuring availability for domestic consumers and adequate opening stock, allocation for diversion of sugar for ethanol is decided,â ISMA functionaries said.On Monday, the average all-India retail prices of sugar stood at Rs 63 per kg, 29% higher than Rs 48.7 per kilo a month back.Speaking to reporters, ISMA president Niraj Shirgaokar said that the increase is not being driven by any âactual shotfallâ in availability. âThe largest contributor has been speculative behaviour. A section of traders created a misleading impression of tightness, and in response, large bulk buyers who would normally procure just-in-time began stocking 1.5-2 months of supply in advance. That behaviour pulled sugar out of circulation and into godowns, creating artificial tightness that had nothing to do with actual availability,â he said.ISMA said that prices have risen also due to factors including lower production than estimated, weather conditions and pests that impacted the crop. The association functionaries said that millers got a good ex-mill price, which peaked Rs 58-59 a kg, due to this artificial rise in sugar prices and now itâs declining, which will soon be reflected in the retail market.Shirgaokar projected the closing stock of roughly 35 lakh tonne at the end of Sept calling it âa healthy buffer against normal domestic demandâ He added govtâs duty-free import window, tightened stockholding limits, ongoing special crushing, and an early start to the new season would help in augmenting domestic supply and control prices.Asked about govt putting blame on industry for jacking up ex-mill prices, ISMA president said that the industry was not involved in creating any artificial scarcity and increasing rates. However, he did not rule out that some mills might be holding stocks and said the govt is looking into that.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Trump admin set to revoke up to 2 lakh visas in historic crackdown
articles.summary: International Business News: The Donald Trump administration is preparing to revoke the business and tourism visas of as many as 2,00,000 foreigners who have applied for or are cu.
articles.body: The Donald Trump administration is preparing to revoke the business and tourism visas of as many as 2,00,000 foreigners who have applied for or are currently seeking asylum in the United States, in what could become the largest single mass visa revocation in US history.The state department is expected to announce the move in the coming weeks, unless the plan is challenged or revised. It would cover B1 and B2 visas issued between 2016 and 2026 to holders who have sought asylum or are currently pursuing asylum, news agency AP reported citing state department documents and US officials.âWe are coordinating with DHS to identify and revoke the nonimmigrant visas of foreigners who have come to the United States claiming to be short-term visitors, but then file for asylum to stay here permanently,â state department spokesman Tommy Pigott said.Pigott did not confirm the number of visas that could be revoked, saying "as the process will be ongoing, the number of revocations remains dynamic and will be done on a rolling basis.âThe revocations would not automatically lead to immediate deportation, officials said. Those with pending asylum cases could retain their ability to pursue those claims but would lose their status as business or tourism visitors.The move is part of the administrationâs broader tightening of US visa and immigration rules since President Donald Trump began his second term. The government has increased scrutiny of applicantsâ social media activity, introduced visa bond requirements and restricted visa issuance to citizens of certain countries.B1 visas are generally issued for business travel, while B2 visas cover tourism, family visits and medical treatment. It was not immediately clear how many current or former B1 and B2 visa holders have sought asylum and would be affected by the planned action.The administration has already revoked about 1,75,000 visas over the past 18 months, including those held by people convicted or accused of crimes such as drunken driving, rape and robbery, as well as some who publicly opposed US policies.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. articles.title: UPI@10: How platform changed the way we pay
articles.summary: India Business News: MUMBAI: Nearly one in two real-time payments in the world happen on the UPI platform. From 1.8 crore transactions in FY17, the year it was launched, t.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Nearly one in two real-time payments in the world happen on the UPI platform. From 1.8 crore transactions in FY17, the year it was launched, to 24,162 crore transactions in FY26, UPI transactions have grown 13,000 times.Today, the payment platform completes 10 years since it went live for general public use after its initial launch by then RBI governor Raghuram Rajan through a pilot test in April 2016. How did the most successful innovation under NDA govt come about?According to AP Hota, founding chief of National Payments Corporation of India, during whose term most of NPCI's products, including UPI, were launched, the idea originated from a dilemma over how to increase the use of IMPS (Immediate Payment Service). IMPS was a real-time payment platform built by repurposing the national financial switch infrastructure created for ATM transactions which required real-time debits from bank accounts. Before IMPS, electronic payments largely mimicked traditional payments, with transactions taking place in batches.Initial brainstorming showed that merchants needed to receive money immediately, which cards could not provide. While IMPS enabled person-to-person transfers, it was not designed for customers who wanted to pull money."UPI began as an attempt to redesign IMPS so as to simplify merchant payments, involve non-bank payment providers, reduce e-commerce payment failures, and adopt open-source technology and APIs. These objectives led us to move away from IMPS and build an entirely new solution, retaining only its proven real-time settlement engine," said Hota."Pramod Verma (technology architect who helped design UPI's API-driven architecture and played a key role in shaping its open, interoperable framework) became involved, while Nandan Nilekani was already with us as our technology and public policy adviser. Pramod and Nandan came up with the idea of making the entire system API-driven, with third-party application service providers," said Hota, who worked with banks and fintech companies to expand the network.Dilip Asbe, current chief of NPCI, who was COO at the time of the launch and led much of the implementation, explained the design in a podcast with Verma in Aug last year. UPI's scale, they said, came from designing it not as a centralised application with a massive database but as a decentralised, open protocol that resolves payment addresses in real time across participating banks.The architects built advanced capabilities into the core protocol while adopting a phased rollout, starting with basic peer-to-peer transfers before introducing features such as recurring mandates.While UPI's scale is now measured in billions of transactions, Hota had forecast in his 2017 farewell speech that the platform would achieve a billion transactions a day within a few years.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. articles.title: Why some US restaurants are banning tips
articles.summary: Tips are central to US dining culture but some eateries think that they are unfair.
articles.body:
Wine waiter Caroline Kraetzer earns $40 (Â£30) an hour, double what most service staff in San Francisco are paid but then it costs a lot to eat at her restaurant.

At a set price of $140 (Â£100) per person, La Cigale is one of a small number of US restaurants charging higher prices so it can pay high salaries - and it doesn't allow tips.

It tells customers: "What you see is what you pay. We do not accept tips, your kind words and return visits will suffice."

Kraetzer says it is good to no longer be "reliant on the generosity of strangers to pay the bills".

While waiting staff at other restaurants can make a lot of money from tips, she says "you're often there two hours before service, and again when you're closing after the guests have left, so you are making minimum wage during that time".

On the other side of the US, Rachel Miller, chef and owner of Nightshade Noodle Bar in the town Lynn, Massachusetts, moved to a tip-free model five years ago when they reopened after the Covid-19 pandemic.

Her motivation was to make it fairer for the kitchen staff.

"The people breaking their backs and minds in the kitchen - often the least visible and the least celebrated - were taking home a fraction of what the front staff made on tips for the same hours," she says.

Miller says she found it "deeply unsettling" to see higher tips going to white male staff and lower tips to everyone else.

"Tipping lets guests, consciously or not, pay people differently based on gender, race, or sexuality and I was not willing to let that decide my team's income."

To pay the staff higher wages, Miller also increased prices at the French-Vietnamese restaurant. Its tasting menus now start from $102 (Â£75) for seven courses before 18:00, and $126 (Â£92) for nine courses.

"Our prices are higher than a comparable restaurant's because they carry the full cost of paying people properly," says Miller. "That is the trade, and I stand behind it."

Yet not every restaurant that has switched to a tipless model has made a success of it, as sometimes customers don't appreciate the higher menu prices.

Talulla in Cambridge, Massachusetts, dropped tips in 2020 so it could pay staff more equitably, only to then switch back in September of last year.

"We tried to keep our non-tipping model simply by raising our menu prices 23%, but we were only able to sustain this through the winter months," says co-owner Danielle Ayer.

"Operating a non-tipped restaurant is more expensive overall," adds Ayer.

This is because tips don't count as part of a restaurant's revenues, but higher menu prices do. So if a venue increases prices to pay staff more, its revenues go up accordingly, and it must pay more sales tax.

William Michael Lynn, professor of food and beverage management at Cornell University and author of The Psychology of Tipping, says the problem of going tip-free is that customers struggle to get their heads around the maths.

"Higher menu prices make dining out seem more expensive because people do not adequately take into account that they are no longer tipping," he says. "It leads to lower demand."

In New York, vegetarian restaurant Dirt Candy was one of the very first to ban tipping back in 2015. "I wanted to make it more equal for everybody," says chef and owner Amanda Cohen, who now pays her staff about $30 an hour.

She says that many customers "are pleasantly surprised when they realise they don't have to tip 20% on top".

Cassidy Van der Kamp is a filmmaker whose YouTube documentary Tipless was inspired by her own experience of working in a restaurant in Oakland, California which went tip-free.

While some other servers left, Van der Kamp, who was originally paid about $10 an hour plus tips, decided to stay and earned $21 per hour after the change.

"I had stability for the first time as I knew what I was earningâ¦ and I didn't need to look at a low tip and think what did I do wrong?"

While Van der Kamp liked the move, Lynn says that a huge challenge of moving to a gratuity-free system is that it can be difficult to attract and retain waiting staff who like getting tips.

However, given the growth of what has been called "tipping fatigue" â people being increasingly annoyed at having to pay high tips â will more restaurants stop the practice?

"Despite tip-fatigue, I do not think tipping is going to be eliminated on widescale anytime soon because the economic disadvantages of eliminating tipping outweigh the advantages," says Lynn.

Back at Nightshade Noodle Bar, Miller doesn't regret her decision. "The clearest measure is that staff stay.

"Turnover in this industry is brutal, and we have people who have been here since we made the change. It has proven to be highly valued by my guests and team."

articles.title: Labour survey 2026 likely to track digital, platform workers
articles.summary: India Business News: NEW DELHI: In a first, India's official statistical machinery is likely to provide data on the digital and platform-based workers in the upcoming annu.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: In a first, India's official statistical machinery is likely to provide data on the digital and platform-based workers in the upcoming annual periodic labour force survey (PLFS), a move which will help policymakers assess the true scope and nature of the fast-growing gig workforce in India, an official told TOI."In PLFS 2026, data on digital platform workers - a subset of gig workers is being collected among the workers classified in the existing PLFS framework as self-employed, regular wage/salaried or casual workers on an experimental basis. All such workers will be included in the broader self- employed category," the official said. The survey results are expected in March 2027 and will provide the maiden official estimate of the number of people working as food delivery executives, drivers and as a myriad of home service providers, among other things in the country.Currently, anyone who engages in market activities for profit is covered under the PLFS framework as a worker, though it does not capture data on people engaged in the gig or digital and platform-based work separately, thus making it difficult to identify gig and platform workers among the total workforce. Drawing upon a 2022 NITI Aayog study, a labour ministry think tank VV Giri National Labour Institute in its latest study expects the gig and platform workforce in the country to grow over 6 crores by 2047 - constituting nearly 15% of the total non-agricultural workforce in the country."Along with enumeration, other key characteristics of such workers, which will include their earnings, working hours, working conditions will also be captured in the upcoming labour force survey. This will help govt to formulate welfare policies for them and implement the provisions of the social security code," the official added.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Government eyes 3000 crore by selling 6% in Hindustan Copper
articles.summary: India Business News: MUMBAI: Govt is selling up to 6% in Hindustan Copper at a floor price of Rs 514 per share through an offer for sale (OFS) to mobilise about Rs 3,000 c.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Govt is selling up to 6% in Hindustan Copper at a floor price of Rs 514 per share through an offer for sale (OFS) to mobilise about Rs 3,000 crore. The floor price for the OFS is at an 11.6% discount to the stock's closing price of Rs 573.6 on BSE on Monday. This is the 10th divestment offer in the current fiscal.According to the company's disclosures on BSE, govt is offering to sell a little over 2.9 crore shares (3% of the company's equity capital) through the OFS, which will open today. Depending on the demand, govt may offer another 2.9 crore shares to investors, it said.Retail investors will be able to bid on the second day of the offer, that is, Aug 26. "10% of the offer is reserved for retail investors, with an additional 25,000 shares reserved for eligible employees," secretary, DIPAM, govt's divestment department, said through a post on X (formerly Twitter).Currently, govt holds 66.1% in the copper miner and producer, shareholding data on BSE showed. Post the successful divestment in the company, govt's stake would come down to a little over 60%. DAM Capital Advisors, Emkay Global Financial Services and IDBI Capital Markets & Securities are managing the offer for govt, the OFS notice on BSE showed. This divestment comes within three weeks of the most successful OFS in India. On Aug 6, govt closed the offer to sell 10% in life insurance major LIC and mobilised Rs 31,515 crore from the market. It was the biggest such offer in India ever.Till date in FY27, govt has mobilised Rs 52,716 crore from nine divestments and some receipts from SUUTI. The Budget had set a Rs 80,000-crore divestment target for the current year.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: VÍDEO: gado foge de incêndio que atinge fazendas; fogo avança por áreas rurais de três estados | G1
articles.standfirst: Em Mato Grosso, 120 hectares de cana foram destruídos; Tocantins e Rondônia também registraram incêndios em áreas rurais.
articles.summary: Em Mato Grosso, 120 hectares de cana foram destruídos; Tocantins e Rondônia também registraram incêndios em áreas rurais.
articles.body:
O tempo seco e as altas temperaturas favoreceram incêndios em áreas rurais de Mato Grosso, Tocantins e Rondônia na última semana.

Em Jangada, no Mato Grosso , o fogo atingiu áreas de plantação e de criação de animais, e o gado precisou fugir das chamas. ( Veja no vídeo acima ).

🗒️ Tem alguma sugestão de reportagem? Mande para o g1

O incêndio causou prejuízos a dezenas de produtores rurais. Alguns, inclusive, tiveram que deixar suas casas.

Uma área de 120 hectares de cana-de-açúcar também foi completamente destruída pelo fogo.

"Tudo aquilo que a gente já fez, vai ter que fazer de novo. Foram duas áreas queimando ao mesmo tempo e a gente ficou sem poder fazer muita coisa", relata Elizamara de Souza, gerente da usina.

Além do clima, rajadas de vento de cerca de 40 km por hora e pastagens sujas, colaboraram para o fogo progredir rapidamente, informou o corpo de bombeiros.

Na fazenda de Dogmar Rockenbach, mais de 40 vizinhos se uniram para impedir que o fogo avançasse na propriedade.

Já em São Miguel do Tocantins , o incêndio destruiu 50 hectares de vegetação em um assentamento onde vivem 150 famílias de agricultores familiares.

Foram mais de 24 horas de combate ao fogo, que foi controlado por agentes da Defesa Civil da região. Não houve registro de danos às propriedades nem de pessoas feridas.

Em Rondônia , o fogo atingiu grandes proporções e afetou propriedades rurais e uma área de preservação ambiental no município de Mirante da Serra. As causas do incêndio estão sendo investigadas.

articles.title: Arrecadação federal soma R$ 289 bilhões em julho, novo recorde para o mês | G1
articles.standfirst: Recorde está relacionado com crescimento da economia brasileira, com aumentos de impostos anunciados nos últimos anos pela equipe econômica do presidente Lula e com tributação e aumento no preço do petróleo.
articles.summary: Recorde está relacionado com crescimento da economia brasileira, com aumentos de impostos anunciados nos últimos anos pela equipe econômica do presidente Lula e com tributação e aumento no preço do petróleo.
articles.body:
A arrecadação do governo federal com impostos, contribuições e demais receitas somou R$ 289,3 bilhões em julho deste ano, informou nesta terça-feira (25) a Receita Federal.

O resultado representa um aumento real de 9% na comparação com o mesmo mês do ano passado, quando a arrecadação somou R$ 265,5 bilhões (valor corrigido pela inflação).

O valor também foi o maior já registrado para meses de junho desde o início da série histórica da Receita Federal em 1995 — ou seja, em 32 anos.

➡️O recorde na arrecadação está relacionado com o crescimento da economia brasileira e com os aumentos de impostos anunciados nos últimos anos pelo governo do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT).

alta na tributação de fundos exclusivos (alta renda) e das "offshores" (exterior);

mudanças na tributação de incentivos (subvenções) concedidos por estados;

aumento de impostos sobre combustíveis feitos em 2023 e mantido desde então;

reoneração gradual da folha de pagamentos;

fim de benefícios para o setor de eventos (Perse);

alta na tributação dos juros sobre capital próprio.

➡️Segundo a Receita Federal, a arrecadação neste ano também tem sido resultado da tributação e da disparada do preço do petróleo. Com um preço mais alto, resultado da guerra entre Estados Unidos e Irã, também subiram as receitas do governo com o produto, como "royalties" e extração. Além disso, o Executivo estabeleceu uma taxação extra sobre exportações.

Postos da região de Bauru começam a receber bombas de combustível antifraude — Foto: TV TEM/reprodução

Nos sete primeiros meses deste ano, ainda segundo dados oficiais, a arrecadação federal somou R$ 1,87 trilhão — sem a correção pela inflação.

Em valores corrigidos pela variação dos preços, a arrecadação totalizou R$ 1,9 trilhão de janeiro a julho, o que representa um crescimento real (acima da inflação) de 7% em relação ao mesmo período do ano passado, quando somou R$ 1,77 trilhão.

O montante também é o recorde para a arrecadação federal no período.

Assim como nos últimos anos, o governo espera contar com o aumento da arrecadação para tentar atingir a meta para as suas contas em 2026.

Para este ano, a meta é de que as contas do governo tenham um saldo positivo de 0,25% do Produto Interno Bruto (PIB), cerca de R$ 34,3 bilhões.

De acordo com o arcabouço fiscal, aprovado em 2023, há um intervalo de tolerância de 0,25 ponto percentual em relação à meta central.

Ou seja: a meta será considerada formalmente cumprida se o governo tiver saldo zero, ou se chegar a um superávit de R$ 68,6 bilhões.

O texto, no entanto, permite que o governo retire desse cálculo R$ 57,8 bilhões em despesas. E use esses recursos para pagar, por exemplo, precatórios (gastos com sentenças judiciais).

Na prática, portanto, a previsão é que o governo tenha um rombo de R$ 23,3 bilhões nos cofres públicos em 2026 – mesmo que, para o cálculo oficial da meta, apresente um resultado positivo.

Se os números se confirmarem, as contas do governo devem ficar negativas durante todo o terceiro mandato do presidente Lula .

articles.title: Meiji Seika to push new vaccine with SII in India
articles.summary: India Business News: TOKYO: Meiji Seika Pharma-owned Medreich Pharma is eyeing inorganic growth and more generics supply from India, while the parent has tied up with Seru.
articles.body: TOKYO: Meiji Seika Pharma-owned Medreich Pharma is eyeing inorganic growth and more generics supply from India, while the parent has tied up with Serum Institute of India (SII) to launch Japanese Encephalitis vaccine in the country."SII will take the required approval to provide the vaccine for children in India. Our subsidiary has already marketed this vaccine in Japanese market. Hopefully, next year SII will apply and try to take the approval in India and then they will market this vaccine," Meiji Seika Pharma COO for pharma segment Toshiaki Nagasato said after a meeting with commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal here on Monday. The Japanese company is seeking that the approval should be accelerated."SII manufactures at the lowest cost. We believe SII will launch the vaccine at affordable and lowest cost. SII technology offcials also came to Japan to understand the technology in Japan," Nagasato said.According to WHO, there are three types of Japanese Encephalitis vaccines, which are given to children. Japan has the technology to help combat the disease that it once grappled with and combined with India's low cost manufacturing capability the partnership could help children. SII and Meiji Seika Pharma had announced the achievement of the first milestone last April.Nagasato said the Japanese company is looking to invest into its Indian subsidiary Medreich, which it had acquired in 2014, although he refused to disclose the amount. He said the idea is to help expand the Indian company's generic operations within the country and also for exports to countries, such as UK, Canada and other European and African companies.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. articles.title: Andy Burnham refuses to rule out tax rises in autumn Budget
articles.summary: Experts have warned that he and Chancellor John Healey will have little room to manoeuvre in their first Budget.
articles.body:
Andy Burnham has refused to rule out tax rises in the upcoming autumn Budget, saying he "won't be unrealistic" about the "challenging" state of public finances.

The prime minister said he would take a "careful approach" to the economy, and defended his previously announced cost of living pledges as funded spending commitments.

Burnham became prime minister in July promising to give people breathing space and help with the cost of living, but questions remain over how major policies such as social care reforms will be funded.

Experts have previously warned that he and Chancellor John Healey will have little financial room to manoeuvre in their first Budget on 28 October.

Speaking during his first visit to Ukraine , Burnham said the policies announced so far including capping bus fares at Â£2 and cutting VAT on household electricity bills were "the first steps that I've felt able to make", and were doable because he was able to reprioritise funding from elsewhere.

"I took the decision early on that digital ID wasn't the top priority for now. And so we've reprioritised funding to other priorities," he said in an interview with ITV.

Asked if the public needed to accept some of the new policies would have to be paid for in tax rises, Burnham said they wouldn't necessarily have to accept that.

Pushed on whether he would need to raise taxes to cover spending gaps, he said: "I will always take a careful approach to things. I ran Greater Manchester for 10 years and we ran a very tight ship with rock solid finances.

"Nothing will change as I come into this role as prime minister. I won't take risks with people's jobs or their livelihoods or their family finances.

"I will try to help them in whatever way I can, I have already done some things that will help them."

Burnham previously told the BBC he accepts his earlier announcements aimed at tackling the cost of living are not enough on their own and hinted at further support.

Speaking during his first official overseas visit on Monday, he said while he would do what he could, "I won't be unrealistic and people really need to understand that.

"We are in a challenging position, whatever I do will be carefully thought through, it will be funded and there will be more to come as we go into the autumn."

Last week official figures showed the the government borrowed more than expected in July , despite a record month for income tax receipts.

Inflation also reached a four-month high of 2.9% in July and is expected to rise further due to the ongoing impact of the Iran war, which has hit energy prices and fuel costs.

Experts have warned Burnham and Healey that they need to either raise taxes or cut spending elsewhere as pressure on the public finances has left no room for extra borrowing.

Both the prime minister and chancellor have vowed to stick to the fiscal rules set by former chancellor Rachel Reeves.

The rules are designed to ensure day-to-day spending is funded through tax revenue by the end of the Parliament, and to reduce debt as a proportion of GDP.

Rain Newton-Smith, chief executive of the Confederation of British Industry, said business owners wanted to create opportunities for young people but "the cost of employing people has gone up so much".

"The business leaders I speak to say that the cost of doing business has gone up so much that it's holding them back from creating opportunities," she told the Today programme.

She said targeted support for businesses would create "more growth and more opportunities that saves money for the government and ultimately leads to higher tax receipts".

articles.title: Trumpâs SpaceX stake: US President invested up to $50,000 in Muskâs company - report
articles.summary: International Business News: US President Donald Trump reportedly invested between $15,001 and $50,000 in Elon Muskâs SpaceX in June, according to a financial disclosure that reve.
articles.body: US President Donald Trump reportedly invested between $15,001 and $50,000 in Elon Muskâs SpaceX in June, according to a financial disclosure that reveals a new financial link between the president and the major government contractor.Trump bought the SpaceX shares on June 23, the disclosure showed, as reported by Reuters. He signed the filing on August 12, and it was made public on August 22. The purchase was among more than 1,000 stock transactions he made during June.SpaceX completed the biggest-ever US IPO on June 12, reaching a valuation of $1.77 trillion and becoming a major player across space, satellite and artificial intelligence markets.The investment comes as the Trump administration takes decisions that could directly affect SpaceXâs business. The company is a US military contractor and regularly requires approvals from federal agencies.On Thursday, Trump directed his administration to help sharply expand the number of commercial space launches in the US. SpaceX is a dominant player in the sector.The White House said Trump does not personally control his investments. Spokesman Davis Ingle told Reuters that third-party financial institutions independently manage the presidentâs portfolio and replicate ârecognized indexes, such as the Schwab 1000.ââNeither President Trump nor any member of his family has any ability to direct, influence or provide input regarding how the portfolio is invested or when investments are bought or sold,â Ingle said.The disclosure also comes amid scrutiny of other Trump administration officialsâ financial ties to Muskâs companies. US Small Business Administration chief and Trump cabinet member Kelly Loeffler earned millions from SpaceXâs IPO, Reuters previously reported.Loeffler initially invested in xAI, Muskâs AI and social media company that later merged with SpaceX. She made a second investment after Trump nominated her to lead the SBA.According to PitchBook analyst Franco Granda, Loefflerâs first xAI investment could have been worth between $7 million and $2.6 billion on the IPO date, depending on the amount and timing of the investment. Her second investment could have been worth between $2.2 million and $25.4 million.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Precio de la luz por horas hoy, martes 25 de agosto: cuándo es más barata y más cara en el día
articles.standfirst: El precio de la luz se encarece notablemente este martes
articles.summary: El precio de la luz se encarece notablemente este martes
articles.body: Hoy, el precio medio de la electricidad se sitúa en 120,35 €/MWh, lo que representa un incremento de 25,32 € en comparación con el día anterior. Este aumento se registra en un martes, donde los consumidores podrían enfrentar tarifas más elevadas. A lo largo del día, las horas más caras y más baratas podrían variar considerablemente, lo que es crucial para planificar el consumo energético. El costo de la luz alcanza su punto máximo entre las 20:00 y las 22:00 horas, donde se concentran los precios más elevados. Durante este bloque de tres horas, se registran valores notablemente altos, con un pico de 224.36 €/MWh a las 21:00. A partir de las 19:00, los precios ya están por encima de los 180 €/MWh, manteniendo una tendencia ascendente hasta alcanzar el máximo mencionado, lo que indica un claro patrón de horas críticas para el consumo eléctrico. La electricidad es más barata durante la madrugada y la mañana, especialmente en las franjas horarias de menor consumo. Las mejores oportunidades de ahorro se concentran entre las 01:00 - 03:00 con precios que rondan los 148.01 € y 156.09 €/MWh y, sobre todo, entre las 10:00 - 16:00, donde los precios mínimos se presentan entre 12:00 - 15:00, alcanzando su valor más bajo de 5.69 €/MWh. Hay una ventana amplia de precios bajos de más de seis horas continuas, favorable para quienes pueden flexibilizar su consumo. En el análisis de las franjas horarias del coste energético, se observa una amplia diferencia entre los precios más bajos y más altos, lo que destaca la gran volatilidad del mercado eléctrico para este día. Este comportamiento es crucial para los consumidores, ya que elige estratégicamente las horas de consumo puede llevar a un ahorro significativo en la factura de la luz.

articles.title: âGut punchâ: What Trumpâs new $103,265 H-1B visa fee proposal means for Indian aspirants
articles.summary: India Business News: H-1B visas, one of the popular talent entry routes into the US for Indians, will soon come at an over 6-digit figure cost. The Donald Trump administra.
articles.body: H-1B visas, one of the popular talent entry routes into the US for Indians, will soon come at an over 6-digit figure cost. The Donald Trump administration on Monday issued a proposed regulation that would make permanent an unprecedented fee of more than $100,000 on new H-1B visas for highly skilled foreign workers.The H-1B programme enables US employers to hire foreign workers trained in specialised fields. It provides for 65,000 visas each year, along with another 20,000 for workers holding advanced degrees, with visas approved for periods of three to six years. Before Trumpâs order, the fees for these visas generally ranged from $2,000 to $5,000.Also Read | Trumpâs new H-1B visa reality for Indians: Unpredictable costs, tougher odds, greater risksWhat is the proposed new move on H-1B visas and why is the Trump administration looking to hike fees? What does this mean for Indian H-1B aspirants?Over $100,000 fee proposal for H-1B visasThe proposed rule from the US Department of Homeland Security, published in the Federal Register on Monday, would establish a permanent fee of $103,265 for H-1B visas. The regulation could be finalized by the end of the year.Trump first introduced the fee on a temporary basis last year, but it was later blocked by a US court. The measure significantly increases the cost of H-1B visas that are widely used by employers in the technology, education and research sectors.A federal judge ruled in June that the fee was unlawful and barred the Trump administration from collecting it. A Boston-based appeals court is now reviewing that ruling, while another court is considering whether a judge was right to reject a challenge brought against the fee by a major business group.The temporary fee increase is due to expire in September, a year after it was introduced.The proposed fee would not cover visas issued to foreign nationals who are already in the US on student visas, a group that accounts for a substantial share of new H-1B recipients. It would also not apply when existing visas are renewed.Also read |Trump admin set to revoke up to 2 lakh visas in historic crackdownTrump, a Republican, and other opponents of the H-1B programme argue that companies abuse the system by replacing American workers with less expensive foreign labour.Business groups and many companies, however, maintain that the programme is necessary because qualified American workers are not available for certain positions and because US businesses need the ability to attract highly skilled talent.The legal challenges argue that Trumpâs authority to restrict entry into the US does not give him the power to override the law that established the H-1B visa programme.The administration has also directed authorities to carry out enhanced vetting of H-1B applicants and proposed changing the visa selection system to give greater preference to workers with higher skills and salaries.Earlier in August, the Department of Homeland Security separately introduced fees of as much as $4,500 for applications to extend the stay of H-1B workers or transfer employees based in other countries to the US.What it means for Indian H-1B aspirantsImmigration experts see the move as a blow to Indian H-1B aspirants, particularly entry-level talent. Though the Trump administrationâs fee is not yet finalised, and if implemented, may be challenged legally, it does reflect on the rising trend of challenges to this route.Xiao Wang, CEO, Boundless Immigration sees this fee as a âgut punchâ for Indian H-1B aspirants, compounding what's already been a brutal year.âThe $103K fee doesn't apply to students changing status inside the US or to in-country employer transfers. It lands squarely on workers coming in from abroad. That's the profile of most Indian IT professionals entering on new H-1Bs,â he tells TOI.âWe saw the chilling effect in the FY2026 cap season even before this rule was codified: India-based IT consulting firms pulled back sharply on external applications because the economics stopped working,â he adds.If this gets finalized, the path to the US for a skilled Indian worker narrows further. The wage-weighted lottery already favors senior candidates.âAdd a $103K entry fee on top, and you're essentially pricing out the early-career engineer who doesn't have a US employer willing to absorb that cost,â Wang explains.Employers have already spent the past year grappling with the prospect of a $100,000 H-1B payment.âThis proposal makes clear that six-figure H-1B costs may not be temporary and may be just the starting point. For startups and smaller companies especially, that could fundamentally change who can afford to compete for global talent,â he adds.K Edward Raleigh, Partner at Fragomen, a global immigration law firm, sees employers becoming increasingly selective about who to pick for the H-1B visa lottery.âThe fee remains a proposal, will be subject to public comment and, if finalized, will almost certainly face an immediate legal challenge. But if it takes effect, employers will become far more selective about whom they enter in the H-1B lottery, and the number of registrations will likely fall significantly,â Raleigh tells TOI.âWe have already seen employers focus more heavily on highly skilled, highly paid workers. A fee of this size would accelerate that shift, making the H-1B route much more difficult for professionals who lack an established relationship with a US employer or a particularly strong or specialized skill set,â he opines.H-1B path getting increasingly tougherFor years, H-1B visas have been the primary route for Indian professionals looking to work in the US, build long-term careers and, eventually, seek a green card. That path has become considerably less predictable over the past two years as changes to the H-1B application and selection criteria have introduced greater uncertainty.Indian professionals nevertheless continue to account for the largest share of H-1B visa recipients. Their presence is particularly significant across engineering, technology, financial services, healthcare and research-oriented industries.The H-1B application process has undergone several changes in recent months, including a new selection mechanism with a wage-weighted system and changes to the rules governing the 60-day grace period.At the same time, the Department of Homeland Security is moving forward with a proposal to remove the 60-day grace period currently available to H-1B workers who lose their jobs. The period gives them time to find another sponsor, change their immigration status or prepare to leave the US.The proposal has not yet become law. If it is implemented, however, losing a job would leave affected workers with a much shorter immigration window and could make them more reliant on their sponsoring employer.One thing is becoming evident: The path to getting an H-1B visa is getting narrower and more unpredictable. Experts say Indian aspirants should rebalance their expectations to be more realistic and look for alternative destinations or US visa options as well.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Inside Sukhna's approach to building cafe brands
articles.summary: India Business News: Ask anyone who runs a restaurant what keeps them up at night, and the answers rarely change. Shrinking margins, a star chef who leaves and takes the s.
articles.body: Ask anyone who runs a restaurant what keeps them up at night, and the answers rarely change. Shrinking margins, a star chef who leaves and takes the signature dish with him. Wastage eating into profits. Quality that swings from one outlet to the next. The daily firefight of staff, supply and service, before a single customer is won.Sukhna: A New Lifeline for India's Food BusinessesIndia is eating differently than it did even three years ago. Quick-service delivery has gone from novelty to expectation. The challenge is how do you serve food that tastes freshly made without losing time? Sukhna makes it possible for such platforms, producing quick-serve dishes to recipe, freezing them at peak freshness and moving them through a cold chain to the dark store, where they are finished and out the door in minutes. The speed belongs to the backend that Sukhna is.A different challenge shows up at brands, where a customer expects the same food every time, in every city. Cooked separately in many kitchens, that consistency is almost impossible to promise. Produced to one recipe in one controlled facility, it becomes the default. Sukhna manufactures to the brand's exact specification and locks in taste and texture through its freezing science, so the dish never depends on which outlet or which cook handled it that day.At this scale, hygiene, safety and quality cannot be aspirations; they have to be guaranteed. That is why Sukhna operates a USFDA-certified facility, holding stringent standards.The founder who invested in the backendSukhna is the vision of its founder, Satvik Ahuja, a former McKinsey consultant who traded strategy decks for the far messier reality of a working kitchen. He built the company on a single conviction: India has never lacked great food ideas, only the manufacturing muscle to scale them without compromise. It is not a lesson he learned in a boardroom; he learned it in a kitchen.His own journey began with NutrioBox, a healthy food cafÃ© built on a mission, where he discovered first-hand how quickly ambition collides with the realities of running a kitchen. Then the pandemic arrived. While the industry scrambled, he moved into frozen and chilled, the only way to keep good food moving when everything else had stopped. Sukhna was born at that moment, out of a problem he had lived through himself.His model is deliberately chef-less and foolproof, engineered so that consistency, hygiene and taste come from systems and science, not from whoever happens to be in the kitchen that day. It is a consultant's faith in systems, applied to an industry that has always run on intuition. It is a founder's belief that the future of Indian food will be won on manufacturing, not marketing.Sukhna is a frozen and chilled solutions partner to a prominent clientele and many more, building customised products across savoury categories, from gravies, biryani, paratha, momos, spring rolls, and kebabs to dips, sauces, beverages and beyond. Every product is made to the brand's exact recipe, frozen or chilled using the right science, and delivered through an unbroken cold chain to their outlets and dark stores.Curious about Sukhna's offerings? articles.title: OnlyFans owner was paid over $700m before his death
articles.summary: The site hosts a range of subscription-based content from cooking to fitness videos, but it is best known for pornography.
articles.body:
The late owner of streaming platform OnlyFans was paid more than $700m (Â£513m) in dividends before his death from cancer earlier this year.

Fenix International Ltd, the British company that owns OnlyFans, made $714m in profit before tax last year, it said in its annual report. This is an increase of 5% from 2024.

The site hosts a range of subscription-based content from cooking to fitness videos, but it is best known for pornography and is credited with transforming online adult content by encouraging personal connection between sex workers and subscribers.

Its owner Leonid Radvinsky, who died earlier this year aged 43 , bought the site from its British founders in 2018.

OnlyFans employs just 47 people. Companies with such high profits rarely have such small staff - for example, British retail giant Marks and Spencer, which employs over 65,000 people, made Â£671m in profit last year.

Fenix International's company results show that it paid dividends of $535m for the year ending 30 November 2025, with further dividends payments totalling $174m between then and 26 March 2026.

Radvinsky, who was born in Ukraine and raised in the US, died on 23 March. The company is now owned by his widow, Yekaterina 'Katie' Chudnovsky.

OnlyFans surged in popularity during the Covid-19 pandemic, landing Radvinsky on Forbes' annual list of billionaires just three years later.

The site is known for the way it encourages creators and fans to connect through livestreams, personalised messages, and direct requests for custom-made photos and videos.

In return for hosting the material, OnlyFans takes a 20% share of all payments.

The site had 132 million paying subscribers and 2.5 million active creators in 2025.

The boom in size and popularity under Radvinsky's ownership also brought scrutiny from lawmakers and regulators over its adult content â a recent BBC Three documentary uncovered allegations of exploitation, coercion and violence committed against OnlyFans creators.

In 2024, British regulators launched an investigation into whether children were accessing porn , an issue that the company at the time blamed on a technical issue.

Ofcom ultimately dropped that probe, but it fined the firm about Â£1m , external for failing to respond accurately to its requests for information about the measures it had in place to check the age of its users, who in theory must be 18 or over.

Creators have also debunked the narrative that making explicit videos on the site is a get-rich-quick scheme.

Keily Blair, the chief executive of OnlyFans, said on Tuesday that the company had paid over $30bn to creators since launching a decade ago.

"OnlyFans provides real opportunities to real people by creating a safe, regulated space where people can monetise their content with a global fan base," she said.

"As a UK-based business we have also made a significant contribution to the UK economy, paying over Â£600 million in corporate taxes from 2016 to date."

articles.title: US sanctions 4 Indian firms under âEconomic Outcastâ over Iran oil and petrochemical trade links
articles.summary: India Business News: The United States has sanctioned four India-based companies over their alleged involvement in Iranâs petroleum and petrochemical trade, as Washington .
articles.body: The United States has sanctioned four India-based companies over their alleged involvement in Iranâs petroleum and petrochemical trade, as Washington expands its newly launched âOperation Economic Outcastâ aimed at cutting Tehranâs financial and oil revenue networks.The US State Department named Portease Partners LLP, Sadashiva Overseas Ltd, PP Softtech Pvt Ltd and Prakrutees Infra Impex India Pvt Ltd among the entities targeted in the latest sanctions action.The measures are part of a broader US crackdown on Iran-linked petroleum traders, procurement networks, intermediaries, shadow-fleet operators and maritime service providers. Washington said the sanctions are intended to restrict the revenue Iran generates through petroleum and petrochemical exports.The State Department accused Portease Partners, an India-based customs broker, of facilitating multiple shipments of Iranian petrochemical products into India.Two Indian nationals identified as designated partners of the company, Indrismiya Asharafmiya Shekh and Harish Ramchandra Rangi, were also blocked.The State Department said, "PORTEASE PARTNERS LLP (PORTEASE) is an India-based customs broker that facilitated the import of multiple shipments of Iranian petrochemical products to India."Portease was designated under Executive Order 13846 for allegedly engaging in significant transactions involving the purchase, acquisition, sale, transport or marketing of Iranian petrochemical products.Sadashiva Overseas was accused of importing approximately $69 million worth of Iranian-origin petroleum products between February 2024 and June 2025.The State Department said, "SADASHIVA OVERSEAS is being designated pursuant to section 3(a)(ii) of E.O. 13846 for knowingly engaging in a significant transaction for the purchase, acquisition, sale, transport, or marketing of petroleum or petroleum products from Iran."PP Softtech was similarly accused of importing approximately $25 million worth of Iranian-origin petroleum products between January 2024 and June 2025. Its director, Prashant Garg, was also designated.The State Department said, "PP SOFTTECH PRIVATE LIMITED (PP SOFTTECH) is an India-based company that imported approximately $25 million worth of Iranian-origin petroleum products between January 2024 and June 2025. PRASHANT GARG is an Indian national and a director of PP SOFTTECH."Prakrutees Infra Impex was accused of importing Iranian-origin petroleum products worth approximately $25 million between May 2023 and February 2026.The State Department said, "PRAKRUTEES INFRA is an India-based company that imported Iranian-origin petroleum products valued at $25 million from multiple companies, including U.S.-designated BONJOURE COMMODITY F.Z.E., between May 2023 and February 2026."There was no immediate comment from the four companies on the US sanctions announcement.US expands pressure on Iranâs oil tradeThe measures against the Indian companies form part of a wider sanctions package targeting Iranâs petroleum and petrochemical trade.Washington said Iranian oil and petrochemical exports are facilitated through shell companies, third-country intermediaries and shadow-fleet operators. It also targeted customs brokers and port agents involved in helping Iranian-origin commodities enter markets in third countries.The State Department said, "Todayâs action targets all the nodes of this illicit trade, and promotes accountability for the buyers, sellers, intermediaries, and service providers that help facilitate Iranâs destabilizing activities."The US also sanctioned entities in TÃ¼rkiye, Hong Kong and Iran as part of the same campaign, including companies accused of importing, exporting or trading Iranian-origin petroleum and petrochemical products.A Hong Kong-based company, Clever Shipping Limited, was also designated over its alleged role in managing a Barbados-flagged crude oil tanker that Washington said had loaded Iranian-origin petroleum on at least six occasions between 2025 and 2026.âOperation Economic OutcastâThe sanctions come as US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced âOperation Economic Outcastâ, describing it as a broader campaign to sever Iranâs financial connections around the world and restrict revenue supporting the Iranian government.The State Department said the latest measures were also intended "to further expose individuals and entities that enabled strikes against U.S. forces and allies and to restrict the revenue that the Iranian regime uses to attack its neighbors, support terrorism abroad, brutally oppress its own people, and hold the global economy hostage."Alongside the oil and petrochemical sanctions, Washington targeted Iran-based entities and senior military figures accused of supporting military procurement and operations.The US also said its Rewards for Justice programme was offering rewards of up to $10 million for information on senior Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps leaders, including Ahmad Vahidi and Ali Abdollahi.Sanctions carry US financial restrictionsUnder the latest measures, property and interests in property belonging to designated individuals and entities that are located in the United States or controlled by US persons are blocked and must be reported to the Treasury Departmentâs Office of Foreign Assets Control.US persons are generally prohibited from conducting transactions involving property or interests in property belonging to designated or blocked entities unless authorised by OFAC or covered by an exemption.The sanctions also extend to entities that are directly or indirectly owned 50% or more by one or more blocked persons.Washington has framed the measures as part of its broader effort to restrict Iranâs petroleum revenues and disrupt the financial networks that support Tehranâs military and procurement activities.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. articles.title: Coca-Cola's new CEO can boast about something that 'Magnificent 7' members Elon Musk and Mark Zuckerberg can't
articles.summary: A big year for Coca-Cola stock holders.
articles.body:
It has been a good start to the CEO reign of Coca-Cola's ( KO ) Henrique Braun, a company lifer who took over the corner office in March.

Shares of the beverage giant are trading at a record high, up 32% year to date alone. What's more, Coca-Cola shares — often thought of as a boring investment because, hey, they sell soda and juice — have outperformed every member of the "Magnificent Seven" tech complex this year, per Yahoo Finance AlphaSpace data.

While Coke's stock has bubbled up, Mark Zuckerberg-led Meta ( META ) is down by 15%, and Elon Musk's Tesla ( TSLA ) is off by 22% (the latter being the worst-performing Magnificent Seven member in 2026).

Score one for the expense-watching middle managers at Coke — a completely different approach than the likes of Meta (aggressively building massive AI data centers) and Tesla (aggressively building robots and robotaxis).

The investment thesis at Coke has been a classic case of an old-school consumer-products business being reinvented, with a heavy dose of cost cuts and safe-haven appeal in an uncertain world.

Coca-Cola posted a solid second quarter, delivering $13.4 billion in net revenue (up 7% year-over-year) and a 16% jump in earnings per share to $1.03.

The outperformance was fueled by a 6% increase in organic revenue and a 5% increase in global unit case volume, driven by high-margin products like Coca-Cola Zero Sugar and by key international growth markets.

Pricing power, operational efficiencies, and favorable currency tailwinds allowed the company to expand its comparable operating margins and raise its full-year earnings guidance.

Furthermore, investors have bid up shares as a premier defensive haven, seeking Coca-Cola's reliable cash flow and dividend stability amid recent market volatility and fluctuating bond yields.

"KO continues to demonstrate why it's the leading large cap global beverage company and deserves a relative valuation ahead of recent history," Evercore ISI analyst Robert Ottenstein wrote in a note. "We believe it is a must own name for long-term income-oriented investors looking for the potential to compound returns at ~10% rate."

articles.title: Kedaara Capital invests $200 mn in Tynor Orthotics
articles.summary: India Business News: MUMBAI: Homegrown private equity (PE) firm Kedaara Capital has invested $200 million in Mohali-based Tynor Orthotics as it looks to take a share of In.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Homegrown private equity (PE) firm Kedaara Capital has invested $200 million in Mohali-based Tynor Orthotics as it looks to take a share of Indiaâs fast-growing medical devices sector. Tynor Orthotics makes a range of orthopaedic supports, mobility aids and rehabilitation solutions. The companies did not disclose the specifics of the transaction but it is understood that Kedaara Capital has picked up a majority stake as part of the funding deal which will also give an exit to Tynor Orthoticsâ existing investor Lighthouse Funds.In a statement, Kedaara Capital said that it will work with the promoters of the company and its early backer Thuasne to expand the brandâs footprint across local and international markets. The strategy will be to build an ortho-focused wellness platform. âIndiaâs medical devices sector is among the fastest-growing in the world, and Tynor represents a rare opportunity to partner with a clear category leader in orthopaedic supports and rehabilitation,â said Sunish Sharma, founder & managing partner, Kedaara Capital.Founded in 1993, Tynor today reaches over 300,000 retail outlets and 8,000 hospitals across 60 countries. Kedaara Capital, which has built a local portfolio across consumer, healthcare, tech services and financial services, had raised a $1.7 billion fund in 2024, among the biggest by a domestic PE firm. It has backed companies including Lenskart, Juspay and Axis Finance. PE deal activity has gathered pace of lateârecently, KKR bought a minority stake in BookMyShow.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
